Let
\[
q=n-r.
\]
I claim the least integer is
\[
\boxed{\left\lfloor \frac{2n-3r-3}{r}\right\rfloor+1 }.
\]

A monomial of \(B\) of standard degree \(d\) has the form \(x^ay^bz^c\) with
\[
a+b+c=nd.
\]
We first characterize when such a monomial lies in \(A\).

A degree-\(1\) generator of \(A\) is concentrated near one vertex of the degree-\(n\) simplex. For example, an \(x\)-type generator has exponent vector
\[
(n-u-v,u,v),\qquad u,v\ge 0,\quad u+v\le r.
\]
Thus if a degree-\(d\) monomial is written as a product of \(d\) such generators, and if \(s_x,s_y,s_z\) are the numbers of chosen \(x,y,z\)-type generators, then
\[
s_x+s_y+s_z=d
\]
and necessarily
\[
a\ge q s_x,\qquad b\ge q s_y,\qquad c\ge q s_z.
\]
Conversely, if nonnegative integers \(s_x,s_y,s_z\) with sum \(d\) satisfy these three inequalities, then the excesses can be distributed among the other coordinates because each generator has exactly \(r=n-q\) units of “off-vertex room.” Hence
\[
x^ay^bz^c\in A
\]
if and only if
\[
\left\lfloor \frac aq\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor \frac bq\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor \frac cq\right\rfloor
\ge d.
\tag{1}
\]

Now take a monomial \(M=x^ay^bz^c\in A_d\), and write
\[
F(M)=\left\lfloor \frac aq\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor \frac bq\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor \frac cq\right\rfloor=d+\delta,
\qquad \delta\ge0.
\]
Let the residues of \(a,b,c\) modulo \(q\) be \(\rho_x,\rho_y,\rho_z\). Before any floor value increases, we can add at most
\[
H=(q-1-\rho_x)+(q-1-\rho_y)+(q-1-\rho_z)
\]
total exponent. Since
\[
a+b+c=nd
\]
and
\[
\rho_x+\rho_y+\rho_z=nd-q(d+\delta),
\]
we get
\[
H=3(q-1)-\bigl(nd-q(d+\delta)\bigr)
=q\delta-rd+3q-3.
\tag{2}
\]

Multiplying by a monomial of \(B_e\) means adding total exponent \(ne\). The smallest possible increase in \(F\) after adding total exponent \(ne\) is
\[
\max\left(0,\left\lceil\frac{ne-H}{q}\right\rceil\right).
\]
Therefore every product \(M\cdot B_e\) lies in \(A_{d+e}\) exactly when
\[
\delta+\max\left(0,\left\lceil\frac{ne-H}{q}\right\rceil\right)\ge e
\]
for all \(e\ge0\).

The worst case occurs when one can add a whole degree-\(1\) monomial of \(B\) without increasing \(F\) enough. The condition for failure is
\[
H\ge n(\delta+1).
\]
Using (2), this becomes
\[
q\delta-rd+3q-3\ge n\delta+n.
\]
Since \(q=n-r\), this simplifies to
\[
r(d+\delta)\le 2n-3r-3.
\tag{3}
\]
But \(d+\delta=F(M)\ge d\). Hence if
\[
d>\frac{2n-3r-3}{r},
\]
then no monomial of \(A_d\) can fail the containment after multiplication by \(B\).

Thus
\[
A_+^mB\subseteq A
\]
holds for
\[
m=\left\lfloor \frac{2n-3r-3}{r}\right\rfloor+1.
\]

It remains to see this is sharp. Put
\[
s=\left\lfloor \frac{2n-3r-3}{r}\right\rfloor.
\]
Choose a degree-\(s\) monomial in \(A\) with exponent vector
\[
(qs,\alpha,\beta),
\qquad \alpha+\beta=rs,\qquad 0\le \alpha,\beta<q.
\]
This is possible because
\[
rs\le 2n-3r-3=2q-r-3<2q.
\]
It is a product of \(s\) \(x\)-type generators, and
\[
F=\left\lfloor\frac{qs}{q}\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor\frac{\alpha}{q}\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor\frac{\beta}{q}\right\rfloor=s.
\]
By (3), there is a degree-\(1\) monomial of \(B\) whose product with it still has \(F=s\), hence is not in \(A_{s+1}\). Therefore \(A_+^sB\nsubseteq A\).

So the least integer is
\[
\boxed{\left\lfloor \frac{2n-3r-3}{r}\right\rfloor+1 }.
\]
